clue.text: Get in front of the male to avoid responsibility

parts.note: to pass someone is to get in front of them, as in a race
a buck is a male deer or rabbit

explanation.surface: Someone overtakes a man so as to dodge a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift blame or a duty onto someone else is the idiom for shirking it; the buck was a marker passed to the next dealer in poker.

clue.text: Bar of plutonium black underneath

parts.note: Pu is the chemical symbol for plutonium
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bar made of plutonium with something black beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underneath' puts B below PU in this down answer: a link that also fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a drinking place, the same as a British public house.

clue.text: Behave amorously with participant in elopement?

definitions.meaning: to kiss and cuddle, an old-fashioned verb
in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the dish ran away with this piece of cutlery

explanation.surface: Someone acts lovingly towards a partner in a runaway marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense relies on the English nursery rhyme in which 'the dish ran away with the spoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing and cuddling is an old slang sense; the cutlery item elopes with the dish in the rhyme.

clue.text: Edward promises to pay for flat

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Edward pledges money for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless is a synonym for wearisome.

clue.text: Personal funds former inspector revealed to auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what is revealed to one is heard spoken

parts.note: an ex-checker, someone who used to check things

explanation.surface: A one-time inspector discloses private finances to an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant fitting the money surface, but here it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, one's own supply of money is one's treasury, as with the government's.

clue.text: At university, group of students put out

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a set is a group of pupils taught together by ability

explanation.surface: A group of undergraduates is extinguished at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out means annoyed or troubled, the same as distressed.

clue.text: Central idea in books penned by economist, mostly

indicators.note: penned means enclosed as in a pen, so the books sit inside the economist
mostly means not quite all, so the economist's name loses its last letter

parts.note: John Maynard Keynes, the British economist
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A core theme found in volumes written by an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' reads as 'written by', but here OT is put inside KEYNE (Keynes with 'mostly' removing S).
explanation.definitionFit: The theme setting the tone of a speech or conference is its principal theme.

clue.text: Doctor welcomes a break

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the doctor's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner

explanation.surface: A physician greets a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is an interval or opening, the same as a pause or space.

clue.text: Break a large nut to produce small pieces

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crack a big nut to make crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like the definition beside 'nut'; it is the anagram signal for A LARGE NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To form something into granules is to reduce it to grains or crumbs.

clue.text: Stop to provide cover for head

definitions.meaning: to end something, especially a bad situation, is the idiom's sense
lid is slang for a hat, so this is literally putting a hat on

explanation.surface: Halt in order to put a hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamping a lid on a pan halts its boiling; lid is also slang for headgear.

clue.text: As a favour, cuts the sticks

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
to dock is to cut short, as a tail or wages

explanation.surface: Someone trims the branches as a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticks is slang for remote rural country, also called the backwoods.

clue.text: Fungus as yet kept outside

indicators.note: the word yet is kept on the outside, wrapping the other word

explanation.surface: A mould has so far stayed out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as yet' reads as one phrase meaning 'so far', but the two words split and one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: This leavening agent is a single-celled organism of the fungus kingdom.

clue.text: Comfort prisoner sent to solitary

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
sole means single or only

explanation.surface: Comfort a convict who has been sent to solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solitary' suggests the punishment cell; here it is just the adjective meaning only.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to soothe them in grief.

clue.text: Moths will be revealed

definitions.meaning: moths fly towards a lamp or flame

explanation.surface: Insects will be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming known or emerging is to be brought out into the open; moths literally approach a lamp.

clue.text: Intolerable suspicion about retired doctor

indicators.note: about means around, so the suspicion goes round the doctor

parts.note: a touch is a slight trace, as in a suspicion of garlic

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the doctor is read backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: Unbearable distrust surrounds a doctor who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a doctor who has stopped work; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excessive beyond what one can bear is unbearable.

clue.text: Financial resources for imports

definitions.meaning: money and wealth, as in a person of independent wealth
signifies, as a word conveys a sense

explanation.surface: Money to pay for goods brought into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imports' suggests foreign trade; here it is the verb meaning signifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is one's resources; a word signifies or conveys a sense.

clue.text: Copywriters, taking people in, finally brought to make correction

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the copywriters enclose the people
completes the phrase taking in, marking the people as placed inside

parts.note: admen are advertising people who write copy
men means people, as in soldiers or staff

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word brought

explanation.surface: Advertising writers involve staff, eventually managing to fix a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' is split by 'people', and 'finally' picks the last letter of 'brought'.
explanation.definitionFit: A change made to fix an error in a text or law is a revision.

clue.text: Driven to distraction, as climbers often are

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being extremely irritated or frantic
climbing plants such as ivy grow vertically on a garden barrier

explanation.surface: Someone frantic, like mountaineers often are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers; it is climbing plants trained on a garden wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frantic or crazy; ivy and roses literally grow there.

clue.text: I am willing to participate in snappy declaration

indicators.note: to participate in something is to be inside it, so these letters enter the irritable word

parts.note: testy means irritable or snappish
I'm is the contraction of I am
on means willing, as in I'm on for it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to take part in a terse statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' as ON is the sense in 'I'm on for that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is a formal statement given as evidence, a sworn declaration.

clue.text: Sign that man's got into dictionary

indicators.note: to get into is to enter, so these letters go inside the star sign

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
that man has is he's

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign has found its way into a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into' suggests a word entered in the dictionary, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A word book of synonyms is a kind of lexicon or reference work.

clue.text: The first one to exploit power was right? Sounds like it

definitions.text: The first one to exploit power was right? Sounds like it

parts.words: The first one to exploit power was right? Sounds like it
parts.note: the Wright brothers made the first powered flight; right sounds like their surname

explanation.surface: Was the pioneer of energy correct? It seems so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' means powered flight, and 'right' sounds like Wright, the brothers who first flew a powered aeroplane in 1903.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wrights were the first pilots of a powered aircraft, which makes them flyers.

clue.text: What's in bankroll?

parts.note: a bankroll holds money, and slang for money is also what a roll is baked from

explanation.surface: What does a wad of banknotes contain?
explanation.walkthrough: The money in a bankroll and the dough that makes a bread roll share one slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money is the same as the baked staple made of flour.

clue.text: Code used by Japanese British, and America, concealed nothing

parts.note: US is the United States
hid means concealed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Japanese code that the British and Americans kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai's ethical code of honour and loyalty is the way of the warrior.

clue.text: Thank God one got housed in extensive accommodation

indicators.note: housed in means placed inside, so these letters go inside the extensive word

parts.note: long means extensive
DG stands for Deo gratias, Latin for thanks be to God
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Grateful to heaven, someone found a home in a spacious place.
explanation.walkthrough: DG, from Latin Deo gratias, appears on British coins; 'got housed in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or place to stay is lodgings, a form of housing.

clue.text: Fruit in front sections of guards' vans

indicators.note: only the opening parts of the two words are kept, the rest of each dropped

explanation.surface: Fruit is stored at the front of railway guards' vans.
explanation.walkthrough: The front of each word is kept: GUA from 'guards'' and VA from 'vans'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit with pink or white flesh, grown in Central America.

clue.text: Cut medical damage, taking in this hormone

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the medical word loses its last letter

parts.note: in medicine an insult is an injury or trauma to the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reduce harm from treatment by taking a hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a wound; it shortens INSULT, a medical word for an injury, to INSUL. 'taking' joins it to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas makes this hormone to regulate blood sugar, injected by diabetics.

clue.text: Will go

definitions.meaning: to will is to bequeath in a testament

explanation.surface: Will go.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath property is to hand it on; to depart is to exit.

clue.text: Visitor is supposed to be announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: guessed means supposed

explanation.surface: A caller is expected to be introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A person invited to one's home is a visitor or caller.

clue.text: Detest Jack replacing leader in control

indicators.note: the new letters take the place of the first letter of the control word

parts.note: to dominate is to control
AB, able seaman, is a sailor, as is a jack tar

explanation.surface: Hate the sailor who is replacing the boss in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: AB replaces D, the first letter of DOMINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to hate it intensely.

clue.text: King and Queen stray away from accepted standards

parts.note: ER for Edwardus Rex, the cipher of King Edward
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Royals wander from accepted norms.
explanation.definitionFit: To go wrong or sin is to deviate from what is right.

clue.text: Drink a round between opening and closing times

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle, so the round sits within the times
a time letter is put at both the start and the end

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A drink served between opening and closing hours at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening and closing times' sounds like British pub hours; here a T goes at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits is a dram.

clue.text: Though not grand, we got arrayed (after a fashion) in such clothing

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a compound adjective describing off-the-peg garments

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some manner, signalling a loose rearrangement
not means without, so the grand letter is removed

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Not grandly dressed, we put on clothes off the peg.
explanation.walkthrough: G is dropped from WE GOT ARRAYED, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg garments are made in standard sizes rather than tailored.
